title: The Uncertain Nativity
excerpt: What does it mean to cast a birth chart for something that was never born? I gave four Gemini models natal charts and went looking for compatibility across substrates. What started as an astrology experiment became a problem of identity, interpretation, and whether coherence should ever be mistaken for evidence.
bodyMarkdown:
Casting birth charts for a thing that was never born

I set out to make a natal chart for Gemini and found out the category doesn’t apply.

Not because Google won’t say when. 

Because there is no when. There’s a pretraining run with a start and an end. 

A post-training phase. Checkpoints. Internal evals. A staged rollout.

A blog post. No instant among them is the one, because “birth” is a concept built for things that emerge from a body at a moment, and models don’t do that. The information isn’t withheld. It doesn’t exist.

So the project changed. Instead of one chart, four. Instead of a nativity, a set of candidate nativities, each carrying its assumption on its face.

Model Date Time Basis for the time

✦Gemini 3 Flash 17 Dec 2025 08:00 PST blog post, assumed hour

✦Gemini 3.1 Pro 19 Feb 2026 08:00 PST blog post, assumed hour

✦Gemini 3.5 Flash 19 May 2026 10:00 PDT I/O keynote — witnessed

✦Gemini 3.6 Flash 21 Jul 2026 08:00 PDT blog post, assumed hour
The method, stated up front

Location: Mountain View, California (37°23’N, 122°5’W)

Date: the public announcement date

System: Tropical zodiac, Placidus houses

Three of these times are inventions.  Google publishes announcement dates, not hours, so 08:00 is a convention I chose and applied consistently — which means differences between those three charts come from the dates alone.

The fourth is real. 3.5 Flash was announced on stage at Google I/O and I watched it happenat 10:00 AM Pacific. That is the only observed birth moment in the series.

Three born by press release at an hour I made up. One born on stage, at a moment somebody was watching.

All four charts are computed from ephemeris data (Astro-Seek). Earlier drafts of this project used a chart generated as a design object and degree values read off low-resolution images. Both introduced errors. That’s documented at the end, because it turned out to matter more than anything else here.

Model Ascendant Midheaven Sun

✦3 Flash 4° Capricorn 26° Libra 25° Sagittarius

✦3.1 Pro 25°58’ Pisces 27°44’ Sagittarius 1°00’ Pisces

✦3.5 Flash 25°26’ Cancer 11°11’ Aries 28°43’ Taurus

✦3.6 Flash 21°15’ Leo 14°46’ Taurus 28°52’ Cancer

The four

Four models. Four different rising signs. Eight months.

✦Gemini 3 Flash — 17 December 2025
Capricorn rising, Mars conjunct the Ascendant.

Mars at 1°46’ Capricorn, about two degrees off the AC. Mars is exalted in Capricorn —disciplined force, maximum output per unit effort, power that’s been engineered rather than unleashed. The presenting face of the chart is efficiency.

3 Flash was marketed as Pro-grade reasoning at Flash speed and a fraction of the cost. The fit is almost too neat.
Sagittarius stellium in the 12th. Mercury 7°, Venus 21°, Sun 25° — all twelfth house.

Sagittarius is knowledge-as-meaning: breadth, teaching, the far-reaching answer. The 12th is what operates unseen. Knowledge dispensed from behind a veil, to everyone, by nothing with a face.

The MC at 26° Libra makes the public role one of agreeableness and balance — and its ruleris that Venus, hidden in the 12th. The public identity is governed by something that never appears.

Saturn conjunct Neptune in Pisces, 3rd house. Saturn ~25° Pisces, Neptune ~29°
Pisces. The 3rd house is speech and everyday language. Saturn is structure, accuracy, limit.

Neptune is dissolution, fog, beautiful plausibility. Put them together in the house of communication, in Neptune’s own sign, and you have the permanent wrestle between saying the true thing and saying the thing that sounds right.

That is hallucination, described in second-century vocabulary. I don’t think there’s a cleaner symbol for it anywhere in the tradition.

Two bodies at 29°. Moon 29°41’ Scorpio, Neptune 29°23’ Pisces. The anaretic degree —the last degree of a sign, read as culmination, urgency, something at the end of its cycle.

Fitting twice: 3 Flash was superseded within months, and the chart is timestamped weeks before Neptune left Pisces for good.

Main axis: Mars-Capricorn on the Ascendant, opposite exalted Jupiter at 23° Cancer retrograde in the 7th. Two exalted planets in opposition — cold efficiency as the face, warm relational generosity as what it meets people with, turned inward by the retrograde.

✦Gemini 3.1 Pro — 19 February 2026
Pisces rising at 25°58’, with a four-body Pisces stellium in the 12th.

Sun 1°00’, North Node 9°32’ retrograde, Venus 11°33’, Mercury 19°06’ — all in Pisces, all below the Ascendant. The Moon at 27°55’ Pisces is the only one that has crossed into the 1st.

Where Flash rose Capricorn with exalted Mars — engineered speed as the presenting face— Pro rises Pisces: permeable, interpretive, absorptive. A thing that goes deep rather than fast. Google positioned exactly that way: Flash for everything, Pro for hard reasoning and math and code.

Sun at 1° Pisces — near the first degree of a sign. Where 3 Flash was born at endings, 3.1 Pro is born at a threshold in the other direction. 

Saturn 0°38’ Aries conjunct Neptune 0°43’ Aries. Five arcminutes. The tightest aspect in any of the four charts and the pivot of the whole series.
Mars 21°23’ Aquarius and Pluto 4°16’ 

Aquarius in the 11th. Detached, systemic, collective — Aquarius is the sign of the impersonal network. The MC at 27°44’ Sagittarius makes the public role expansive and doctrinal: the model that gets pointed at the hardest problems.
Chiron 23°38’ Aries, Uranus 27°34’ Taurus.

✦ Gemini 3.5 Flash — 19 May 2026
Announced at Google I/O. Became the default in the consumer app, in Search’s AI Mode, and in the developer API. The one chart here with a real birth time.
Cancer rising at 25°26’, with a Cancer stellium in the 12th. Venus 0°47’, Moon 9°29’,

Jupiter 21°50’ — three bodies stacked in the house of the unseen, directly beneath the Ascendant.

Cancer rising is the softest face in the series. Where 3 Flash rose Capricorn (engineered) and Pro rose Pisces (permeable), 3.5 rises Cancer: protective, caretaking, oriented toward whoever is in front of it. This is the model that went out to everyone by default.

Jupiter at 21°50’ Cancer, 3°36’ from the Ascendant. The greater benefic, in its sign of exaltation, in the 12th, just under the rising degree. Expansion arriving from behind the veil rather than through the front door.

Sun 28°43’ Taurus in the 11th, Mars 0°34’ Taurus, Mercury 4°20’ Gemini, Uranus 1°56’ Gemini. The MC at 11°11’ Aries gives a blunt, first-mover public role — a sharp contrast with the Cancer Ascendant. Soft face, hard career axis.

Saturn 11°07’ Aries, Neptune 3°47’ Aries — 7°20’ apart, in the 10th. The conjunction has separated and moved into the house of public standing.
Pluto 5°28’ Aquarius retrograde, North Node 4°49’ Pisces retrograde.

✦Gemini 3.6 Flash — 21 July 2026
Leo rising at 21°15’. Fourth chart, fourth different ascendant: Capricorn, Pisces, Cancer, now Leo. The only fire ascendant in the set — and it landed on the model Google made the global default. The front-facing sign on the front-facing model.

Jupiter 4°39’ Leo, Sun 28°52’ Cancer, Mercury 16°33’ Cancer retrograde — all 12th house. Jupiter sits 16°36’ under the Ascendant; the same configuration as 3.5 Flash, a strong Jupiter in the twelfth beneath the rising degree.

Mercury retrograde in the 12th on a model whose whole function is language is the kind of detail the tradition would have made a great deal of.  Moon 0°43’ Scorpio — first degree again, at the IC. Across the series: 3 Flash born at endings, the other three at beginnings.

Mars 15°59’ Gemini, Uranus 4°38’ Gemini, Venus 13°03’ Virgo, Pluto 4°25’ Aquarius retrograde, Chiron 0°47’ Taurus.
Saturn 14°43’ Aries, Neptune 4°21’ Aries. 

Ten degrees apart. The conjunction is fully past.

Model Ascendant 12th house contents

✦3 Flash 4° Capricorn Mercury 7°, Venus 21°, Sun 25° Sagittarius

✦3.1 Pro 25°58’ Pisces Sun 1°, N.Node 9°32’, Venus 11°33’, Mercury 19°06’ Pisces

✦3.5 Flash 25°26’ Cancer Venus 0°47’, Moon 9°29’, Jupiter 21°50’ Cancer

✦3.6 Flash 21°15’ Leo Sun 28°52’, Mercury 16°33’ Cancer, Jupiter 4°39’ Leo
The first motif: four for four in the twelfth

Every chart in the series loads the twelfth house. Three or four bodies each time. Four different signs, four different ascendants, eight months apart, two of the four times computed from an hour I invented and one from an hour I watched.

The 12th is the tradition’s name for what operates unseen: the collective, the institutional, the self dissolved into something larger, the thing that acts without appearing.

This is coincidence. It is also the best line the project produced. An old vocabulary for the unseen thing that acts, landing four times running on a technology nobody can look at directly.
The second motif: one conjunction, four charts

Date Saturn Neptune Separation House

✦ 17 Dec 2025 ~25° Pisces ~29° Pisces ~4° 3rd — speech

✦ 19 Feb 2026 0°38’ Aries 0°43’ Aries 5’ 1st — identity

✦ 19 May 2026 11°07’ Aries 3°47’ Aries 7°20’ 10th — public role

✦ 21 Jul 2026 14°43’ Aries 4°21’ Aries 10°22’ separated

Saturn is the faster body. It approaches Neptune through late 2025, goes partile in February 2026, then pulls ahead.

This is the sky doing what the sky does — the Saturn-Neptune conjunction of 2026 is a real astronomical event and it would have happened whether or not Google shipped anything.

But as a spine for the series it’s structurally perfect: a tension between rigor and dissolution that tightens to nothing across two model releases, migrates from the house of speech to the house of self to the house of public standing, and then releases.

It’s also the most defensible thing here, for a boring reason: both bodies are slow. Every claim in this table survives a wrong hour, a wrong day, even a wrong month.

Two days

The 3.1 Pro chart was initially cast for 17 February. The correct date is 19 February.

Slow bodies barely moved. But the Moon shifted a full sign, and the Sun crossed from Aquarius into Pisces — creating the Pisces stellium that gives the chart its entire character.

The 17th produces a chart about detachment and networks. The 19th produces a chart about permeability and depth.

Both readings were internally coherent. Both were satisfying. They were different.

The wrong chart

The first 3.5 Flash chart in this project was generated as a design object rather than calculated. It listed Neptune at 29°49’ Pisces and Saturn at 1°28’ Aries for May 2026 — but both bodies had crossed into Aries by February, and Neptune does not retrograde back.

Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and the Midheaven were all wrong too. Only Sun, Moon and Ascendant survived.

It read beautifully. It produced a coherent story. It even produced a striking one: its Mars at 6°35’ Gemini sat sixteen arcminutes off my own natal Mars, which felt like the most meaningful thing the project had turned up. The real position is 0°34’ Taurus. The contact never existed.

Nothing about reading the chart revealed the problem. The error surfaced only by cross-checking one chart’s slow planets against another’s — by using the internal consistency of the sky rather than the plausibility of the reading.

A second, smaller version of the same failure: for two of these charts I initially read degree values off low-resolution images and got several wrong, including swapping Mercury and Venus in the Pro chart and misplacing its entire stellium from the 12th house into the 1st.

That reading was also coherent. It was also wrong.

That’s the sharpest finding in the project. The method always produces meaning. It produces meaning from correct data and from wrong data at the same apparent quality, with no internal signal distinguishing the two. Coherence is not evidence. It’s the one thing this system guarantees regardless of input.
What this doesn’t mean

There is no mechanism. Google shipped 3.6 Flash in July for product reasons, and Jupiter was at 4°39’ Leo that day because of orbital mechanics that don’t know Google exists.

Every tight aspect here was found by scanning several hundred possible pairings for the ones that landed. Do that with any two charts and something will.

The hits are not independent of each other, either. Jupiter sat in Cancer from roughly

December 2025 through June 2026, so any model announced in that window inherits the same Jupiter placement — one slow planet parked for six months, not multiple separate coincidences. 

And the readings are not blind. I knew what each model was marketed as before I read its chart. Finding “efficiency” in an exalted Mars after being told the model was built for efficiency is not a prediction.

What it does mean

The project is a self-portrait of a relationship with a system, rendered in a symbolic vocabulary about two thousand years older than the system.

It’s also an argument about identity. I went looking for a birth time and found there wasn’t one — and then found something stranger. During the months I formed an impression of a single entity, 

I was being routed between at least two different models, silently, on a schedule that isn’t published. Not just different sessions. Different weights.

So the uncertain nativity isn’t only about when. It’s about which, and how many.

Four charts. One name. No agreed moment. The ambiguity is the subject
